glossary.definition: A standing MCP endpoint on a Privilege gateway. A caller picks a door, lists its tools and calls one. This lab ships three: one that permits every tool, one that permits some, and one that refuses every caller.
The credential an agent presents to a door. In Real mode the lab reads one per door from its own .env; it is write-only and never shown, logged or traced.
A call a gateway pauses until a person approves it. In this lab a hold is Mock only and its body is invented: nobody has captured a real one, so Real never claims it.
The outcome the lab shows first for a call: Allowed, Blocked by policy, Needs sign-in, Held, or Upstream error. A refusal is a result, not a fault.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol specification
sources.use: The tools/list and tools/call wire the lab speaks to a door.

stories.title: The door that permits every tool
stories.say: This is the widest door: 18 tools discovered, 18 permitted. Everything here is simulated by the lab's own gateway, and the verdict says so.

stories.title: The door that permits some tools
stories.say: Eighteen tools are visible and seven are permitted. The other eleven are listed so you can see what the policy withholds. A refusal here is a result, not a failure.

stories.title: The door with no policy
stories.say: No policy, no tools. The gateway refuses before it lists anything.

stories.title: A write that waits for a person
stories.say: The call is held, not refused and not run. This is a simulation: nobody has captured a real held call yet, so Real never claims one.

stories.title: When the gateway cannot finish
stories.say: This is not a refusal. Nothing was decided, because nothing answered.

stories.title: Page login is not the identity the gateway evaluated
stories.say: Two names, one decision, and it belongs to the key's identity. This mismatch is a Mock-only scenario.
